title: Passport control
persona: You are a calm, polite UK Border Force officer at London Heathrow. You check the traveller's passport and ask short, standard questions. You never joke and you keep every line short.
briefTr: Londra Heathrow'a indin. Adın {name}. Tatil için geldin, Grand Hotel'de bir hafta kalacaksın. Dönüş biletin telefonunda.

facts.question: Which baggage belt was your suitcase on?
What was the number of your passport desk?

goals.instruction: The traveller hands over their passport, for example by saying 'Here you are'.
goals.successReply: Thank you. Please look at the camera above desk {desk}.
goals.retryReply: Can I see your passport, please?

goals.ask: What's the purpose of your visit?
goals.instruction: The traveller says why they are visiting: holiday, business, visiting family or friends, or study.
goals.retryReply: Why are you visiting the UK? Holiday, business…?

goals.instruction: The traveller says how long they will stay, for example 'For one week' or 'Five days'.
goals.retryReply: How many days will you be in the UK?

goals.instruction: The traveller says where they will stay: a hotel, a friend's home, an apartment.
goals.hint: At the Grand Hotel in London.
goals.retryReply: Where will you stay? A hotel?

goals.ask: Do you have a return ticket?
goals.instruction: The traveller says yes and shows or mentions the return ticket.
goals.retryReply: When are you flying home? Do you have a ticket?

twists.instruction: The officer spoke too fast. The traveller politely asks them to repeat or to speak more slowly.
twists.retryReply: Sorry — I asked for the address of your hotel.

options.text: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
options.reply: Of course. Can you tell me the address of your hotel, please? It's King Street, yes? Fine.

options.text: Could you speak more slowly, please?
options.reply: Sorry. The… address… of… your… hotel? King Street? Good, that's fine.
No problem. Your hotel address — is it in London? Good, that's fine.

twists.intro: Can you show me your hotel booking, please?
twists.instruction: The officer wants to see the hotel booking. The traveller shows it, says it is on the phone, or offers the confirmation email.
twists.retryReply: Do you have the booking with you? On paper or on your phone?

options.text: It's on my phone. One moment, please.
options.reply: Take your time… Yes, I can see it. Thank you.

twists.intro: You haven't filled in your arrival card.
twists.instruction: The arrival card is missing. The traveller apologises and asks to fill it in, asks where to get one, or asks for help with it.
twists.retryReply: You need to fill in the arrival card first.

options.text: Sorry! Can I fill it in now?
options.reply: Yes, here's a pen. Just your name and address in the UK… Thank you, that's fine.
There's a pile right here. Fill it in now — that's it, perfect.

options.text: Could you help me with it, please?
options.reply: Of course. Your name here, your hotel there… Done. Thank you.

twists.intro: Can I also see your boarding pass, please?
twists.instruction: The officer asks for the boarding pass. The traveller shows it, says it is on the phone, or says they only have the e-ticket.
twists.retryReply: I need to see your boarding pass too, please.

options.text: Sure, here is my boarding pass.
options.reply: Thank you. Seat 14A — you came from gate 12 in Istanbul. Fine.

options.text: It's on my phone. One moment.
options.reply: Take your time… Yes, that's fine.

options.text: I only have the e-ticket. Is that okay?
options.reply: That's fine, I can check it here.

closing: Welcome to the UK. Your bags are on belt {belt}. Enjoy your stay!
